chrome.guestNotice: Sign in to save your results
chrome.guestSaveBanner: You're browsing as a guest — this profile is only saved in this browser and will be lost if you clear your data or switch devices.
chrome.footerTagline: Client-side and private — your results never leave your browser.

landing.eyebrow: Four lenses. About three minutes each.
landing.titleLead: The parts of you that keep showing up,
landing.titleAccent: no matter which test you take
landing.subtitle: One quiz asks how your mind works. Another asks how you're wired under pressure. A third asks what people clock about you in the first five minutes. Take any combination — we'll show you where they agree, and it's usually more than you'd expect.

combined.title: Where Your Four Lenses Agree
combined.body: {count, plural, =0 {Take your first quiz below, and we'll start sketching who you are.} =1 {One lens down, three to go — and it's already telling us something. Here's a preview.} other {# of 4 lenses in. They're starting to agree on some things — see where.}}
combined.cta: {count, plural, =0 {See What We Know So Far} =1 {See What We Know So Far} other {Bring It All Together}}

pairing.title: Better With Someone Else's View
pairing.body: Build your combined profile, then invite a partner, friend, or family member to compare theirs against yours — see exactly where you click and where you clash.

forTeams.title: See how your team actually works together
forTeams.subtitle: Colevitate combines four personality frameworks into one composite view of a team — where everyone clusters, where the team is spread thin, and where someone might need to deliberately cover the gap. Private by default: each person opts in before their results are shared.

frameworks.title: One view, four frameworks
frameworks.body: 16 Personalities, Big Five, Human Design, and Color Type, combined into a single composite read on how your team actually operates — not just four separate quiz results.

optIn.title: Opt-in, never mandatory
optIn.body: Nobody's results are visible to the team until they explicitly choose to share. Team leads see the composition, not anyone's raw answers.

anySize.title: Built for any team size
anySize.body: Works the same for a 3-person pod or a 30-person department — invite people with a code, and the composition view fills in as they join.

forTeams.secondary: Have an invite code? Join a team instead.

mbti.label: 16 Personalities
mbti.description: Sixteen types, one four-letter read on how you focus your energy, take in the world, and make up your mind. Most people finish this one nodding.

bigfive.label: Big Five
bigfive.description: No types to squeeze into — five traits, scored on a real spectrum, in your own words. The closest thing here to a second opinion on yourself.

humandesign.label: Human Design
humandesign.description: We left out the birth chart. What's left: ten questions about how you actually make decisions and spend energy — whether you wait to be asked or go first — through Human Design's lens on operating styles.

colors.label: 4 Color Types
colors.tagline: What people clock in five minutes
colors.description: Before anyone learns your type, they read this: are you driving the room, studying it, holding it together, or lighting it up? Four styles, one fast, honest snapshot.

assessments.meta: {count, plural, one {# question} other {# questions}} · ~3 min

survey.remaining: {remaining, plural, =0 {No questions} one {# question} other {# questions}} left · ~{minutes} min

guidance.body: Answer based on what you naturally do — not what you think you should do, or what you've trained yourself to do. There are no good or bad answers here.

accuracyOffer.title: You've got a usable result already
accuracyOffer.body: Want higher accuracy? {remaining, plural, one {# more question} other {# more questions}} (~{minutes} min) will sharpen the close calls. Or finish now with what you've already answered.

reflection.placeholder: What made it hard? (kept private, used only to improve the questions)
reflection.sent: Thanks — noted privately, it'll help us improve this question.
